title: Ethiopian Black-Eyed Pea Stew
localName: ሽምብራ ዓይን ወጥ — Shimbra Ayin Wat
community: All of Ethiopia — the black-eyed pea fasting stew
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Black-Eyed Pea Stew — black-eyed peas (cowpeas) slow-cooked in a berbere and onion sauce. One of the more affordable fasting legume stews — black-eyed peas require less soaking time than chickpeas and provide a creamy, earthy texture in the berbere sauce.
longDesc: Black-eyed pea stew is an important part of Ethiopia's fasting cuisine repertoire — cowpeas grow well in Ethiopian lowlands and provide an affordable, highly nutritious protein source for fasting periods.
ingredients: 2 cups dried black-eyed peas — soaked 4 hours
steps: Boil soaked peas 35—40 minutes until tender.
Add oil and berbere. Fry 3 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes.
chefTips: Black-eyed peas require shorter soaking and cooking than chickpeas.
They should remain slightly firm — unlike lentils which dissolve.
cookingScience: Black-eyed peas contain trypsin inhibitors — anti-nutritional factors that are deactivated by boiling. Pre-soaking and boiling removes most of these compounds, making the peas' protein fully bioavailable.
sustainabilityTips: Black-eyed peas are drought-resistant and grow in Ethiopian lowlands without irrigation.
culturalNote: Black-eyed pea stew extends the fasting platter's legume variety — providing a different texture and flavour profile from lentils and chickpeas, ensuring that fasting days offer genuine food diversity.
